lemmas.gloss: CAMIL's/Makransky & Lilleholt's route from presence through interest/motivation/self-efficacy to learning outcomes.
Kreijns et al.'s named CSCL design pitfall: assuming social interaction occurs simply because the environment permits it.
a user's graphical self-representation within a virtual environment.
the theory that people apply social rules to media/computers themselves.
a room-scale, projection-based immersive VR system, used in ped-sec-33's studies.
Mayer's multimedia-learning design principle: exclude extraneous material.
Sweller's framework distinguishing intrinsic, extraneous, and germane processing demand.
the route from presence/agency through extraneous cognitive load to (negative) learning outcomes.
the Community of Inquiry's construct for meaning-construction through sustained reflection/discourse.
Mayer's dual-channel, limited-capacity model of multimedia learning.
Kreijns et al.'s named CSCL design pitfall: designing solely for task/cognitive processes, neglecting the social-affective dimension.
inflation risk when subjective mediator and outcome measures share an administration method.
Garrison, Anderson & Archer's three-presence (cognitive/social/teaching) framework for online educational transactions.
a popular (and often-critiqued) hierarchy of learning-retention-by-modality.
a sub-factor of social presence: the felt salience of other participants in a mediated space.
Gunawardena & Zittle's finding that social presence can be actively fostered within a medium, not just fixed by it.
HMD-induced nausea/disorientation/eye strain from sensory-conflict during VR use.
structured, repeated, feedback-driven skill practice; a Strand-D professional-education design principle.
Radianti et al.'s fourteen-category coding scheme for IVR application design features.
Fowler's pedagogy-first (vs. technology-first) approach to VR-learning design.
the idea that added task friction (e.g., VR motor cost) can, within limits, support learning.
the account that IVR's sensory richness competes for attention with learning content.
the claim that a learning intervention's effect is stable across deployment settings when medium is held constant.
the three-way partition of cognitive load in generative-learning-adapted CTML.
the finding that instructional supports helpful for novices can hinder more knowledgeable learners.
task-irrelevant cognitive load induced by high-fidelity or entertaining-but-irrelevant stimuli.
VanderMeer et al.'s named set of VR-collaborative-learning affordances.
sustained absorptive engagement in an activity matched to skill/challenge level.
the select-organize-integrate model of active learning processing.
a standardized quality-of-evidence rating system used in systematic reviews.
Gunawardena & Zittle's Likert scale operationalizing social presence for CMC, with intimacy/immediacy/affective-association/co-presence sub-factors.
a standardized-mean-difference effect-size statistic, bias-corrected for small samples.
psychological/communicative closeness conveyed through verbal and nonverbal cues; a SPRES sub-factor.
Witmer & Singer's companion instrument measuring individual differences in tendency to become immersed.
interpersonal closeness/warmth conveyed in mediated communication; a SPRES sub-factor.
Fowler's caution that increasing technological affordance may help learning only up to a point, then hurt it.
Joanna Briggs Institute standardized tools for assessing study quality in systematic reviews.
a four-level (reaction/learning/behavior/results) framework for evaluating training outcomes.
Makransky et al.'s own summary phrase for the presence/enjoyment-vs-outcome dissociation.
the Medical Education Research Study Quality Instrument, used to grade simulation-education study quality.
the communication-theory account that a medium's bandwidth/cue-richness determines its capacity to convey interpersonal presence; explicitly rejected by Garrison, Anderson & Archer.
Clark's (1983) argument that instructional method, not delivery medium, drives learning outcomes.
the distinction between presence experienced through a communication medium and unmediated (face-to-face) presence.
Mayer's design principle: present words as narration rather than on-screen text when paired with graphics.
a virtual environment supporting concurrent multiple users.

lemmas.term: Nature and Determinants of Presence Model (NDPM)
lemmas.gloss: Chow's SEM-derived model of presence's psychological determinants.
the risk that early enthusiasm for a new technology inflates short-term outcome measures.
Lombard & Ditton's core definition of presence: a failure to perceive/acknowledge the existence of the medium.
Mayer's design principle: conversational rather than formal tone improves multimedia learning.
the process-model component underlying the Community of Inquiry's cognitive presence (triggering event → exploration → integration → resolution).
Mayer's design principle: teach names/characteristics of key components before the main lesson.
the standardized reporting framework for systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
Mayer et al.'s own organizing structure for weighing IVR's benefits against its risks.
the distinction between an environment's actual capability and a user's perceived capability.
Mayer's design principle: avoid presenting identical information in both narration and on-screen text.
making an abstract concept perceptible/tangible in a virtual environment.
the degree to which a virtual environment perceptually resembles its real referent; one of Dalgarno & Lee's core affordances.
Gunawardena's finding that already socially expressive communicators show compensatory socio-emotional expression online.
a statistical technique for testing hypothesized causal path structures among latent constructs.
engaging but task-irrelevant content/stimuli that impose extraneous cognitive load.
Mayer's design principle: break content into learner-paced segments.
the standard cybersickness self-report instrument, originally designed for flight-simulator contexts; its fitness for HMD-VR is contested by Cossio et al.
Walther's account that CMC users adapt to channel limitations over time rather than being permanently constrained by them.
reduced individual effort in group settings, a named risk for VR-collaborative learning.
the sense of others as meaningfully present/salient in a mediated communication; this cluster's Strand-F-grounding construct.
a metaphor, cited by Biocca et al., for treating social presence as a continuously adjustable rather than binary property of a medium.
Short, Williams & Christie's origin theory; the shared ancestor of every Strand-F unit.
instructor behaviors that reduce psychological distance from students; linked to satisfaction in CMC contexts.
the Community of Inquiry's construct for instructional design, facilitation, and direct instruction.
Davis's model of perceived usefulness and ease of use as predictors of technology adoption/use.
the cognitive/associative/autonomous stage model of procedural skill learning, relevant to Strand D.
publication-bias diagnostic techniques used in meta-analysis.
a study design manipulating instructional features *within* a medium rather than comparing across media.
the illusory sensation of self-motion induced by visual stimuli, relevant to cybersickness.
an interactive, screen-mediated simulated-patient scenario used in health-professions education.
the composite latent construct combining representational fidelity and interactivity/immediacy of control in several Strand C SEM models.
a media-user variable (not a system property) contributing to presence, per Lombard & Ditton.
see *Inverted-U*.
newly formed groups with no prior shared interaction history, relevant to CSCL social-interaction pitfalls.
